stages.Planning: Analysis of the existing project, audit report review, gap analysis and refurbishment plan

entries.title: Analyse the audit report
entries.prompt: Extract the text of SplitStack_Comprehensive_Technical_Audit.pdf (61 pages) and summarise its findings: technology stack, architecture, route inventory, database schema, security findings (SEC-01..SEC-07), test results, technical debt and the five-phase refurbishment roadmap (Phases A-E). entries.title: Gap analysis and refurbishment plan

entries.title: JavaScript architecture and app shell
entries.prompt:
Step P1 (Review 2): JavaScript architecture and app shell.
Add vanilla JavaScript to the Review 1 pages as native ES modules.
1. Add data-page="<page-name>" to the <body> of index.html and every file in client/pages/ (e.g. data-page="dashboard", data-page="expense-form"). Load one entry script at the end of each page: <script type="module" src="../js/app.js"></script> (index.html: src="js/app.js").
2. Create client/js/ with:
- app.js: entry point. Reads document.body.dataset.page, initialises the shared UI, then dynamically imports ./pages/<page>.js if it exists and calls its exported init(). A missing page module is not an error.
- core/dom.js: qs, qsa, on, delegate, createEl helpers.
- core/format.js: formatINR(paise) using Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', {style:'currency', currency:'INR'}), formatDate / formatRelativeDate helpers.
- ui/theme.js: dark / light / system toggle saved in localStorage, applied to <html data-theme>. Add a tiny inline script in each page's <head> that applies the saved theme before first paint (no flash). Wire it to a theme button in the topbar (add the button if missing, matching existing button styles).
- ui/nav.js: replace the CSS checkbox drawer with a real <button aria-expanded aria-controls="sidebar">. Close on Escape, scrim click and nav-link click; trap focus inside while open; return focus to the button when closed. Keep the page usable without JS.
- ui/toast.js: accessible toasts (role="status", aria-live="polite"), auto-dismiss, dismiss button.
- ui/confirm.js: a <dialog>-based confirm that replaces window.confirm for every delete button/form.
3. Add client/js/package.json containing {"type": "module"} so Node (used for unit tests later) treats these files as ES modules.
4. All wrapped in try/catch where localStorage is touched (private windows can throw).
entries.purpose: Establish the client JavaScript ES module foundation, theme switching, accessible drawer, toast notifications, and confirm dialog.
entries.result: Created client/js architecture with DOM/format utilities, theme toggle (dark/light/system with head flash-prevention script), accessible mobile drawer with focus trap and ARIA attributes, toast notifications, and dialog-based confirm. Added data-page, inline theme scripts, theme buttons, and app.js script tags to all 25 HTML pages while preserving no-JS CSS fallbacks.
entries.verification: html-validate passes with 0 errors across client/**/*.html; node automated assertions pass for formatINR, formatDate, formatRelativeDate, HTML structure, and CSS layer definitions; static client preview verified over HTTP on localhost:5500.

entries.title: Client data layer backed by localStorage
entries.prompt:
Step P2 (Review 2): client data layer backed by localStorage.

Create client/js/data/ with:
- store.js: keeps collections (users, categories, expenses, income, budgets, recurring, groups, sharedExpenses, settlements, shoppingLists, receipts, insights) in localStorage under one versioned key (e.g. "splitstack:v1"), generates ids (crypto.randomUUID), handles a missing/corrupt store by reseeding, and has a reset() used by a "Reset demo data" button on the profile page.
- seed.js: the SAME sample data the Review 1 pages show. Read the HTML pages (dashboard, expenses, income, budgets, recurring, categories, groups, group-detail, settlements, shopping, shopping-detail, profile) and transcribe their data: demo user Priya Raman, October 2026, the groups (incl. Goa Trip) and their members, the shopping lists and items. Add a few earlier months so analytics has history. Amounts in integer paise. Demo login: demo@splitstack.app / Demo@1234 (show this on login.html).
- api.js: async functions with the shape the future REST API will have, grouped as auth (register, login, logout, currentUser, updateProfile, changePassword), expenses and income (list with filter/sort/pagination, get, create, update, remove), categories, budgets, recurring (incl. toggle), groups (list, get, create, addMember, removeMember, leave, sharedExpenses, balances, settlements, recordSettlement), shopping (lists, items, toggleItem, convertToExpense), analytics (monthlySummary, byCategory, forecast, insights) and search(query). Every function returns a Promise, validates its input and throws an ApiError {field, message, status} for bad input, missing records or records owned by someone else. Passwords: hash with crypto.subtle SHA-256 + salt (demo only; note in a comment that the server uses bcrypt). Page code must import ONLY from api.js, never from store.js.
- Write a short JSDoc block above each function describing arguments and return value. These docs become the contract the Review 3 REST API must match.
entries.purpose: Create a complete, modular, resilient client data layer with realistic seed data and REST-shaped async API functions, preparing the application for full interactivity without requiring a backend server.
entries.result: Implemented store.js with versioning (splitstack:v1), corruption recovery, and in-memory fallback; seed.js with Priya Raman sample data in integer paise across all collections and historical months; api.js with 58 JSDoc-documented async functions covering auth, CRUD, group splitting balances, shopping lists, and analytics; updated login.html with demo credentials callout; documented data layer in client/README.md; added automated tests.

Proceed to P4: Forms, validation and CRUD flows.

First, inspect the P4 instructions in the handover PDF and review the existing page modules, client/js/data/api.js, client/js/core/, client/js/ui/, and the current HTML forms.

Implement:
1. Connect the login and registration forms to the existing authentication API.
2. Connect expense creation and editing, income creation, group creation, shared-expense creation, shopping-list creation, and other forms specified by P4.
3. Implement client-side validation with accessible field-level errors, appropriate required fields, valid dates, valid integer-paise amounts, and clear error messages.

6. Preserve form values when validation or API operations fail.
7. Use the existing confirmation dialog for destructive operations and ensure cancellation never changes data.
